title: Red meat enhances the colonic formation of the DNA adduct O6-carboxymethyl guanine: implications for colorectal cancer risk
authors: Lewin MH, Bailey N, Bandaletova T, Bowman R, Cross AJ, Pollock J, et al.
population: Healthy volunteers living in a metabolic suite; randomised crossover of a 420 g/day red meat diet and a vegetarian diet, with a high-fibre red meat diet in 13
funder: Grant support: UK Medical Research Council grant-in-aid and UK Food Standards Agency.
authorConflicts: One author is affiliated with Pollock and Pool Ltd., Reading, UK; the article states no role for the company and contains no conflict-of-interest statement.
result: Faecal apparent total N-nitroso compounds, vegetarian against red meat diet: 699 ± 120 against 4923 ± 1387 μg/kg (P < 0.0001); output 193 ± 43 against 667 ± 141 μg/day (P = 0.0002). Exfoliated colonocytes staining positive for O6-carboxymethylguanine: 22.7 ± 2.6% against 55.7 ± 3.3% (P < 0.001); faecal N-nitroso compounds correlated with the percentage of positive cells (r = 0.56, n = 55). The red meat was prepared to minimise heterocyclic amine content.
